replies.author: zayelion
replies.body:
Took me a while to understand and I had to try it myself.

You take a bunch of particles and lay them over an image and then make them glow. You match the color to the image. You then move the points in space to make the image 3d. You get a fluffy paint rushed look there after instead of the smooth look caused by polygons.

replies.author: LiquidZebra
replies.body:
lol, lol, YOU don't do anything, you clone a repo and point AI at that and give it a picture reference and come back 30 minutes later. Ask it to take "two steps" into the scene and all the defects become manifest. 

It is very good for static scenes like the one here (solid objects), it's very bad for scenes with complicated geometry, like a bottle or a cup or a fruit on the table, a column, etc.

replies.author: Slow_Yogurtcloset388
replies.body: Instead of having a big 3d surface you paint with textures, you have thousands of tiny surfaces that takes on colors. Super inefficient. You are trading memory (textures) for compute (tons of little objects to render).

replies.author: Good-Acanthaceae-136
replies.body: Not really, splats are much more resource intensive than just using 3d models. Using splats for this is kind of silly as people tend to use pixel art because it's easy going on hardware.
